title: Observability dependency matrix and migration plan
summary: Inventory and stepwise migration plan to standardize Prometheus/Grafana + OTEL collector topologies in VPC/on-prem private deployments, plus a dependency matrix mapping Terraform modules, ingress controls, and long-term storage options.
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects an inventory of dependent services, a compatibility/impact matrix, and a pragmatic migration plan for private observability stacks (Prometheus + Grafana + OTEL collectors + log shipping) used in Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Target audience: platform engineers, infra TF owners, SREs supporting customer private installs, and solutions engineering for customer cutovers.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus on private-deployments only: VPC-hosted private control plane and on-prem appliance installs. Not the hosted API.
- Includes metrics (Prometheus scraping + remote_write), dashboards/provisioning (Grafana), collectors (OpenTelemetry Collector flavors), and log forwarding (Fluent Bit / Fluentd / syslog adapters).
- Terraform touchpoints: module boundaries, variable surfaces, and state migration considerations.
- Security constraints: customer-managed TLS, KMS/HSM for secrets, and restricted egress.

Current-state quick inventory (examples across recent installs):
- Prometheus: v2.33 and v2.34 variants in customer clusters; scrapes via kube_sd + static targets for on-prem. Remote_write endpoints used for long-term storage: S3-backed Thanos sidecar in some installs, Cortex in others.
- Grafana: provisioned dashboards using provisioning yaml + k8s-configmap; Grafana v9.x in most, v8.x in legacy. LDAP auth used by large enterprise customers.
- OTEL Collector: two main flavors observed: otel-collector-contrib (batch + tail sampling) and small gateway-only collectors. Some installs rely on vendor-compiled collectors with custom processors.
- Log shipping: Fluent Bit on nodes -> central Fluentd in aggregator cluster -> Kafka or object store. Syslog adapters used in isolated networks.

Dependency matrix (high-level, callouts):
- Prometheus scrape config -> depends on service discovery (kube_sd vs. static) and on collector-side metrics exposition (some apps only expose via otlp-metrics).
- Remote_write retention -> depends on long-term storage choice (Thanos/Cortex) and S3/MinIO compatibility + object lifecycle policies.
- Grafana provisioning -> depends on secrets backend (K8s secrets vs. Vault) + LDAP/SSO config (will affect rollout order).
- OTEL Collector topology -> choice of gateway vs. sidecar affects network policy requirements and terraform module surfaces (ingress/egress rules).
- Log pipeline -> implications for throughput (Fluent Bit vs Fluentd), storage (S3 lifecycle), and alerting thresholds in Prometheus.

Compatibility notes (observed breakpoints):
- Prometheus v2.33 -> v2.37: remote_write protocol stable, but relabel_configs edge cases changed behavior for empty label drops. Test suites must include relabeling regression tests.
- Grafana dashboards: provisioning API stable, but folder permission model changed between some 8.x and 9.x minor versions — ensure datasource UID pinning in TF/grafana provisioning.
- OTEL Collector processors: custom processors compiled into contrib builds may not be present in upstream releases; prefer explicit operator-managed extensions rather than baked binaries where possible.

Terraform module map (what to change and why):
- modules/obs/prometheus: split into (a) core-server, (b) scraper-configs, (c) remote-write-backend. Rationale: customers often need to swap remote storage without touching scrape configs.
- modules/obs/grafana: parameterize auth backend (ldap|sso|local) and provisioning source (git|configmap). Add datasource UID override variable to avoid drift.
- modules/obs/collector: add topology_mode variable (gateway|sidecar). When gateway, create dedicated ingress/egress TF resources and service account scopes.
- modules/obs/logs: provide output variables for ingestion endpoints used by Fluent Bit and instruments for downstream capacity planning.

Migration plan (phased) — minimal-customer-impact approach:
Phase 0 — preflight (0-2 weeks):
- Run dependency scan across private-install TF states to enumerate which customers use Thanos vs Cortex vs none.
- Automated inventory: scrape configs, grafana version, collector image digests, log sink types.
- Create a test matrix mapping sample customer topologies to the compatibility matrix below.

Phase 1 — infra modularization (2-6 weeks):
- Land TF refactor: split prometheus module as suggested and provide compatibility variables. Keep old module aliasing for existing state to avoid forced replacement.
- Add feature flags in modules: remote_write_enabled, collector_topology.
- Publish a migration guide (module-level) for customers.

Phase 2 — staged upgrades + smoke tests (rolling, 4–12 weeks):
- For non-critical customers, schedule upgrade windows and run canaries: upgrade Prometheus instance in a sandbox, run relabel and scrape regressions, validate remote_write ingestion at target store.
- Upgrade Grafana only after provisioning UID pinning validated.
- Replace vendor-customized collectors with operator-managed contrib builds where required; validate config equivalence.

Phase 3 — log pipeline hardening and throughput tuning (parallel, 3–8 weeks):
- Deploy load-test harness that replays log volume + metric spikes; measure CPU/memory and backpressure behaviour for Fluent Bit/Fluentd.
- Tune batching and buffer limits; codify sensible defaults in TF variables.

Phase 4 — cutover and rollback plan (per-customer):
- Prepare per-customer preflight checklist: backup grafana db, snapshot Prometheus TSDB, export dashboards, capture collector config.
- Cutover steps: 1) enable remote_write to new store in parallel (dual-write), 2) verify time-series ingestion and alert firing parity, 3) update TF to switch default remote read/write endpoints, 4) reconcile dashboards and permissions, 5) decommission old endpoint after 30d.
- Rollback: revert TF variable for remote_write endpoint, restore grafana snapshot if dashboards mismatch, reintroduce old collector image.

Testing matrix (examples to include in CI):
- Scrape/reglabe tests: synthetic exporters with edge-case labels and high cardinality.
- Remote_write smoke: ensure samples per second and labels preserved.
- Grafana provisioning: ensure datastore connectivity with LDAP + service token rotation test.
- Collector conformance: wave a standard set of OTLP envelopes through gateway and sidecar modes, validate spans/metrics/logs appear in target backends.

Operational play notes (practical tips observed):
- When egress is restricted to whitelisted endpoints, prefer a push gateway or gateway collector that centralizes external writes; avoid per-node remote_write to external S3/Cortex.
- Use UID pinning for datasources in Grafana provisioning to avoid accidental datasource duplication on re-provisioning.
- For customers on older Prometheus versions, enable remapping relabel configs behind a feature-flag and run the mapping in a dry-run mode that writes a shadow label for verification.
- Rotate collector configuration secrets via Vault dynamic secrets where possible; minimize TF-managed static secrets in shared states.

Resource and cost considerations (rough):
- Prometheus TSDB memory scales with scrape target cardinality; double-check scrape intervals and target cardinality during capacity planning.
- Fluentd memory can spike with unbounded buffering; prefer Fluent Bit at edge and Fluentd only for aggregation if heavy enrich/transform required.

Open risks and decisions required:
- Decide standard long-term store for private deployments: Thanos (S3-friendly) vs Cortex (S3 + ingesters) vs customer-managed TSDB. This choice changes TF surface and operational runbooks.
- Policy for vendor-built OTEL collector binaries vs operator-managed containers.
- Required retention defaults (30d vs 90d) and who pays for object storage.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Create a TF-state scanner to enumerate current observability topology per customer (owner: Omar).
- [ ] Draft a module-splitting PR for modules/obs/prometheus with backward-compatible outputs (owner: Marisol).
- [ ] Build small on-prem test harness that simulates restricted egress and run collector topology tests (owner: Nina).

Appendix: quick TF snippet suggestions (example strings only):
- variables.tf for collector topology: variable "collector_topology" { type = string default = "gateway" description = "gateway|sidecar topology for OTEL collector" }
- prometheus outputs to avoid state drift: output "scrape_config_map_name" { value = kubernetes_config_map.prom_scrape.metadata[0].name }

Notes to reviewers: aim feedback at the compatibility matrix and the phased migration durations. The objective is to reduce forced recreates in TF state and make upgrades reversible with minimal customer impact.
